summary.oneLiner: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Limited is a leading Indian manufacturer of plastic extrusion machinery with a strategic, fast-growing new energy division (GEON) focused on lithium-ion battery packs and energy storage solutions.
summary.business: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Limited operates through two core segments. Its legacy Extrusion Machinery business manufactures plastic extrusion systems for pipe and blown film/flexible packaging applications, serving domestic and international customers. The GEON division designs, integrates, and manufactures lithium-ion battery packs for electric vehicles (2W, 3W, 4W, CV) and stationary energy storage applications, operating a technology-agnostic model with in-house R&D.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.

themes.title: PVC piping & building finishing
themes.need: Polymer-pipe and home-finishing plays are driven by agri/plumbing/real-estate finishing demand and PVC resin spreads - distinct from the value-added STEEL-tube structural/capex thesis.
themes.driver: Agri/plumbing/real-estate finishing demand and PVC resin-spread normalization.

hero.oneLiner: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Limited is a leading Indian manufacturer of plastic extrusion machinery with a strategic, fast-growing new energy division (GEON) focused on lithium-ion battery packs and energy storage solutions.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Limited is a leading Indian manufacturer of plastic extrusion machinery with a strategic, fast-growing new energy division (GEON) focused on lithium-ion battery packs and energy storage solutions.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Limited operates through two core segments. Its legacy Extrusion Machinery business manufactures plastic extrusion systems for pipe and blown film/flexible packaging applications, serving domestic and international customers. The GEON division designs, integrates, and manufactures lithium-ion battery packs for electric vehicles (2W, 3W, 4W, CV) and stationary energy storage applications, operating a technology-agnostic model with in-house R&D.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Extrusion Machinery:** Pipe extrusion systems, Blown film/flexible packaging extrusion systems, Multi-layer film technologies, High-output energy-efficient extrusion systems
- **New Energy (GEON):** Lithium-ion battery packs for 2-wheelers, Battery packs for 3-wheelers, Battery packs for 4-wheelers and high-voltage applications, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Telecom and solar storage solutions, C&I energy storage, B2C lithium-ion inverter batteries

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Plastic pipe manufacturing (water, sanitation, agriculture, construction)
- Flexible packaging (food, pharmaceutical, consumer goods)
- Electric vehicles (2W, 3W, 4W, commercial vehicles)
- Stationary energy storage (telecom, solar, C&I, power backup)
- Global exports across 100+ countries

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained global demand driven by transformative shifts in manufacturing environments, evolving end-user industry requirements, stricter regulatory compliance, and a heightened emphasis on sustainable and high-efficiency production processes.
- Rising demand for high-speed film production and flexible packaging solutions, fuelled by consumer preferences for lightweight, durable, and sustainable packaging.
- Government initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission and Smart Cities Mission, expansion in agricultural irrigation, and rising real estate developments in tier-2 and tier-3 cities driving demand for plastic pipes.
- Union Budget 2026-27 emphasis on infrastructure-driven growth, raising capital expenditure by 9% to ₹12.2 lakh crore, with focus on manufacturing, railway expansion, and digital infrastructure development.
- MSME Support & Growth Fund of ₹10,000 crore and a ₹2,000 crore top-up for the Self-Reliant India Fund to facilitate easier capital access for manufacturers.
- Increased outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme to ₹40,000 crore, expected to boost demand for plastic components used in electronics.
- New ₹10,000 crore, five-year Container Manufacturing Scheme to enhance domestic container production, driving demand for plastic products in the logistics sector.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Invest in digital transformation and flexible, high-performance equipment to lead the next phase of expansion in plastic extrusion machinery.
- Prioritize automation, energy efficiency, and precision control to boost production efficiency and minimize downtime.
- Deploy advanced, intelligent extrusion systems through investments in multilayer extrusion technologies and high-barrier films for specialty packaging.
- The Board has formulated and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy in terms of Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, available on the Company's website.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not describe any specific capex project, capacity expansion, or new plant commissioning with a timeline. The MD&A discusses industry growth and budget support but contains no company-level expansion plan.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established market leadership in domestic plastic extrusion machinery with over four decades of experience and a strong installed base across 100+ countries.
- Early mover advantage in India's EV battery ecosystem with 400,000+ battery packs deployed and operational manufacturing since 2020.
- Technology-agnostic, asset-light approach in the energy business, sourcing cells globally while focusing on design, integration, and system optimization, reducing technology risk.
- Strong in-house R&D and engineering capabilities, with a dedicated team of 100+ engineers for the energy business enabling customization for Indian conditions.
- Diversified business model with dual growth engines: a stable, cash-generating extrusion business and a high-growth new energy division.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geopolitical instability and energy price volatility — Escalation of conflict in West Asia and global supply-side shocks have led to sharp volatility in energy prices, directly impacting input costs and demand conditions for the company.
- Global economic slowdown and subdued trade — Projected moderation in global GDP growth to 3.1% in 2026, weaker demand, and softening world trade volume growth could reduce export orders and overall demand for extrusion machinery.
- Inflation persistence and tighter financial conditions — Renewed supply-side pressures are projected to push headline inflation to 4.4% in 2026, leading to cautious central bank policies and tighter financial conditions that may increase borrowing costs and dampen investment.
- Supply chain reconfiguration and higher input costs — Ongoing reconfiguration of global supply chains and higher transportation and input costs could strain margins and disrupt the availability of critical components for machinery manufacturing.
- Regulatory and compliance pressures in end-user industries — Stricter regulatory compliance and heightened emphasis on sustainable production processes in the plastics industry may require continuous investment in technology upgrades, impacting profitability.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Invest in digital transformation and flexible, high-performance equipment to lead the next phase of expansion in plastic extrusion machinery.
- Prioritize automation, energy efficiency, and precision control to boost production efficiency and minimize downtime.
- Deploy advanced, intelligent extrusion systems through investments in multilayer extrusion technologies and high-barrier films for specialty packaging.
- The Board has formulated and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy in terms of Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, available on the Company's website.
